hindi: वह मैथुन में केवल वात को छोड़ता है।
english: In sexual union it releases only Vāta (wind-humour).
notes: Subject 'tat' is carried from the preceding unit (not in this chunk); what 'it' refers to is not stated here. Vāta is kept as the humour (doṣa); the line does not say whether plain 'wind' is meant.

hindi: जब वह पूरी तरह हानि पहुँचाता है, या हानि न पहुँचाते हुए ही स्रोत के मुख को ढक देता है,
english: When, however, it wholly damages, or, without damaging, simply closes the mouth of the channel (srotas),
notes: Subject not stated in the line (carried from earlier context, not in this chunk). GROUPING: 78 and 79 appear to form one 'yadā ... tadā' sentence. 'upahaṃti' is the printed spelling of upahanti. srotas (channel) is kept as a doctrinal term.

hindi: तब वह संस्कार से बाहर हो जाता है। वहाँ संस्कार है: वाजीकर बस्तियाँ यानी वाजीकर एनिमा, अभ्यवहार और चित्त को हर्षित करने वाले भी।
english: Then (he) becomes outside refining treatment (saṃskāra). There the treatment is aphrodisiac (vājīkara) enemas (basti), internal administration (abhyavahāra), and mind-gladdening (ones) too.

text_flags.why: possible: a stray space splits 'harṣaṇāni' (n. nom. pl. 'gladdening'); sense and the following 'ca' fit one word

notes: The subject of 'bhavati' is not stated. 'saṃskārabāhya' is read 'outside (the scope of) refining treatment'; the sense 'treatment' for saṃskāra is taken from 'tatra saṃskāraḥ'. 'vājīkarā bastayaḥ' is regular sandhi (visarga dropped before b). The list is: aphrodisiac enemas, internal administration, and gladdening (ones). 'basti' = enema here.

hindi: तब आसेक्य। स्त्री और पुरुष वैसे ही प्रकार के हो जाते हैं। तब वह वक्रध्वज यानी टेढ़े शिश्न वाला हो जाता है; उसका ध्वज यानी शिश्न कभी कड़ा नहीं होता।
english: Then āsekya. The woman and the man become of that kind. Then he becomes vakradhvaja (one with a bent dhvaja, the penis); his dhvaja (penis) is simply not made stiff.
notes: GROUPING: 82 appears to continue 81. 'tadā''sekyaṃ' (double avagraha as printed) is read tadā + āsekyam; āsekya appears to be a technical name but the line does not define it, so it is left untranslated and the reading is not firm. 'dhvaja' (banner) is a euphemism for the penis (standard). 'vakradhvaja' is read as a bahuvrīhi naming a type. The 'then ... he' clauses have no stated subject.

hindi: जब दुर्गन्धयुक्त योनि वाली स्त्री का गर्भ होता है,
english: When an embryo (garbha) arises of a woman with a putrid vagina (yoni),

hindi: उस शुक्र के आस्वाद से ध्वज यानी शिश्न का उठना पाता है।

notes: Unsandhied print 'āsvādāt dhvaja' (final t not changed to d); recorded as a print habit, not flagged. Subject 'he' is not stated. 'ucchrāya' = raising, erection (probable).

hindi: जब पुमुरुभावपि तत्सौगंधिकारण्यं — ये छपे रूप अस्पष्ट हैं और अनुमानित पाठ पर ही कुछ कहा जा सकता है — तब योनि और ध्वज की गन्ध से बल पाता है।
english: When 'pumurubhāvapi tatsaugaṃdhikāraṇyaṃ' (printed forms unclear; on a conjectural reading only), he obtains strength from the smell of the yoni and the dhvaja.

text_flags.why: possible and not firm: 'pumuru-' is not a word; 'pumān ubhau api' is only a guess

'yonidhvajagandhena' is read as smell of the yoni and the dhvaja (dvandva); 'smell of the dhvaja of the yoni' is also possible. 'dhvaja' = penis (standard euphemism). hindi: जब पुरुष गर्भ में वायु और अग्नि के दोष से वृषण यानी अण्डकोष का नाश होता है, तब वह वायुपिण्डक नाम वाला होता है।
english: When, in the male embryo, there is destruction of the testes (vṛṣaṇa) through the fault of wind (vāyu) and fire (agni), then (it) becomes the one called vāyupiṇḍaka.
notes: 'puruṣasya garbhasya' is read 'of the male embryo'; the line does not say 'in' but the genitive carries it. 'doṣa' here is read 'fault' (not the humour), because it is joined with agni and vāyu in a compound. vṛṣaṇa = testis (standard); the plural or dual is not marked in the compound. 'vāyupiṇḍaka' is a type name, left untranslated. Subject of 'bhavati' not stated.

hindi: कर्म की विचित्रता से ये आठ षण्ढ-योनियाँ यानी नपुंसकों की आठ प्रकार की उत्पत्तियाँ संकीर्ण यानी मिश्रित कही गई हैं।
english: These eight kinds (yoni) of ṣaṇḍha (the impotent), because of the variety of action (karma), are said to be mixed.
notes: Printed 'ṣaṃḍha' is an orthographic form of ṣaṇḍha (recorded once, not flagged). 'saṃkīrṇāḥkathitāḥ' is printed as one token without the expected space. 'yoni' is read as 'kind/origin'. 'Mixed' (saṃkīrṇa) may also be read 'miscellaneous'. The text does not here list the eight.

hindi: जब स्त्री के रक्त और गर्भाशय को दोष थोड़ा दूषित करते हैं, तब जो गर्भ होता है, उस गर्भ के माता से उत्पन्न जिस-जिस अवयव के बीज में या बीजांश में दोष प्रकोप को प्राप्त होता है, उस-उस अवयव में विकृति प्रवेश करती है।
english: When, however, the doṣas slightly vitiate the woman's blood (śoṇita) and uterus (garbhāśaya), then in the embryo that comes to be, whichever mother-born part (avayava) of that embryo has its doṣa reach provocation in the seed (bīja) or in the seed-portion, into that very part a deformity (vikṛti) enters.
notes: 'mātṛjasyāvayavasya' is genitive, read as the possessor of the seed or seed-portion. Doctrinal terms doṣa, bīja, avayava are kept. 'garbhāśaya' = uterus (standard). Constructions 'yasya yasya ... tam tam' are distributive ('each such part').

hindi: जब इसके गर्भाशय में स्थित शोणित नामक बीज में निर्वर्तक बीज दूषित होता है, तब वह बन्ध्या को उत्पन्न करता है।
english: When, indeed, in her seed called blood (śoṇita), situated in the uterus (garbhāśaya), the forming seed (nirvartaka bīja) is vitiated, then it produces a barren one (vandhyā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ra' appears inserted ('ākhye' = called); the same insertion is seen in 'śukarārakhye' (97); 'śoṇita-ākhye' fits the sense

notes: Token 'yadā hyasyāḥ' = yadā + hi + asyāḥ. The subject of 'janayati' is not stated ('it', the vitiated seed). 'Barren (vandhyā)' is the feminine as printed; the noun 'woman' is not in the text. 'nirvartaka' = that which brings about or forms (the body), the line does not say more. The two uses of 'bīja' (the blood-seed, and the forming seed) are as printed.

hindi: जब उसका अवयव, तब — छपा रूप तदापूतप्रजां अस्पष्ट है, अनुमानित पाठ पर बिगड़ी हुई सन्तान वाली —

hindi: जब फिर वह अवयव और स्त्री को बनाने वालों के, तथा शरीर में आश्रित अधोगुरुता आदि के निर्माता जो बीजांश हैं, उनका एक देश,

words.gloss: mṛṇāsuliṅgā (a name; printed form kept, meaning unclear)

hindi: इसी प्रकार पुरुष के विषय में भी, जब शुक्र नामक बीज में बीज दूषित होता है, इत्यादि जोड़ लेना चाहिए: बन्ध्य, बिगड़ी हुई सन्तान वाला, तथा पुरुष की आकृति की प्रधानता वाला, अपुरुष, जिसका नाम मृणासुलिंगा है, उसे उत्पन्न करता है। इसके द्वारा, माता से और पिता से उत्पन्न अवयवों की विकृति के व्याख्यान से, सात्म्य से, रस से और सत्त्व से उत्पन्न अवयवों की विकृति भी समझा दी गई होती है।
english: In just the same way, for a man: 'when, in the seed called śukra, the seed is vitiated' and so on, one should apply it: a barren (one), one of spoiled offspring; and likewise (one) mostly of male shape, a non-male, named mṛṇāsuliṅgā, it produces. By this explanation of the deformity of the mother-born and father-born parts, the deformity of the parts born of sātmya (what suits), of rasa and of sattva (mind) is explained too.

notes: The first part is a quotation ('when ... iti') of the pattern of 91, applied to the man. 'mṛṇāsuliṅgā' is a name after 'nāma'; its meaning is unclear and the print may be corrupt, so it is left untranslated. Several tokens are printed without spaces (bījaṃpraduṣyatītyādiyojayedvaṃdhyaṃ, puruṣākṛtiprāyamapuruṣaṃmṛṇāsuliṃgā, cāvayavānāṃvikṛtivyākhyānena). 'vandhyam' is read as an accusative object (a barren male), 'pūtiprajam' as 'of spoiled offspring' (conjectural). sātmya = what suits one, habit; rasa here is nutritive fluid (probable); sattva = mind (standard); each tagged as the standard reading. hindi: और जब गर्भ पाई हुई स्त्री — अनक्षम् छपा रूप अस्पष्ट है, अनुमानित पाठ पर निरन्तर — वातकारक पदार्थों का सेवन करती है, तब उसका प्रकुपित वायु शरीर में सरकता हुआ गर्भाशय में ठहरकर गर्भ में जड़ता, बहरापन, गूँगापन, नकियापन, हकलापन, लंगड़ापन, कुबड़ापन, बौनापन, अंगों की कमी और अंगों की अधिकता, या कोई दूसरा वात का विकार उत्पन्न करता है।

'garbhasya' goes with the long compound ('in the embryo ... states of ...'); the suffix -tva applies to the whole list. 'minmiṇa' (nasal or indistinct speech) is probable. 'hīnāṅga' (deficient in limbs) and 'adhikāṅga' (excessive in limbs) are as printed. Vāyu is Vāta (standard).

english: Kapha, however: kuṣṭha (leprosy and related skin disease), kilāsa (probably vitiligo), the unclear printed 'sadaṃtavā', and so on.

text_flags.why: possible and not firm: 'sadaṃtavā' is not a word; 'kilāsa-adantatva' (toothlessness) is a guess from similar letters

notes: Elliptical: no verb (understood from the preceding units and not supplied). 'śleṣmā' is the nominative of śleṣman. kuṣṭha (standard) and kilāsa (probable) are identifications; kuṣṭha here may mean a group of skin diseases. The third member is unclear and left untranslated.

hindi: छपा रूप त्रिवर्गौमिश्रान् अस्पष्ट है; अनुमानित पाठ पर विकार।
english: Disorders (vikāra), the printed 'trivargaumiśrān' being unclear (on a conjectural reading only).

text_flags.why: possible and not firm: stray 'au'; 'tri-varga-miśra' (mixed with the three groups) is a guess, so no reading is built

notes: Unclear and elliptical. 'miśrān vikārān' (mixed disorders) and 'tri-varga' (a group of three, possibly the three doṣas) are possible, but the line is not firm. GROUPING: 103 appears to complete the statements of 101 and 102 (Vāta, Pitta, Kapha and mixed).

hindi: और भी।
english: Moreover.
notes: Printed 'apica' = api + ca, a transition formula. GROUPING: introduces 105.

hindi: दृष्टि के भाग को न पहुँचा हुआ तेज जन्मजात अन्धापन है। वही वात से अनुगत हो तो विकृत, रूखी, अरुण आँख वाला; पित्त से अनुगत हो तो पिंगल आँख वाला; कफ से अनुगत हो तो सफ़ेद आँख वाला; रक्त से अनुगत हो तो लाल आँख वाला।
english: Light (tejas) that has not reached the share of sight (dṛṣṭibhāga) is congenital blindness (jātyandhatva). That same, followed by Vāta, has deformed, dry, reddish eyes; followed by Pitta, tawny eyes; followed by Kapha, white eyes; followed by blood (rakta), red eyes.

text_flags.why: possible: the avagraha after 'śleṣmā' is a slip for the compound form 'śleṣma-anugatam' and the space is missing between the two words

notes: 'tejas' is fire or light; the line does not say 'in the eye', and the elemental sense is not applied. 'dṛṣṭibhāga' is read as 'the portion of sight'. The adjectives 'vikṛtarūkṣāruṇākṣam' etc. agree with 'jātyandhatvam' (neuter). 'rakta' may be blood or redness; 'followed by rakta' is rendered 'blood' and the Hindi follows. Closing 'iti' not translated. 'jātyandha' = blind from birth (standard).

hindi: क्योंकि गर्भिणी का गर्भ के समान योगक्षेम होता है।
english: For the pregnant woman (garbhiṇī) has the same welfare (yogakṣema) as the embryo.
notes: 'yogakṣema' (attainment and preservation) is read as 'welfare'; it is a bahuvrīhi qualifying 'garbhiṇī'. GROUPING: 106 and 107 appear to be one reasoning ('for ... therefore').

hindi: इसलिए विशेष रूप से उसकी प्रिय और हितकर से, गर्भ को हानि पहुँचाने वालों से, रक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: Therefore one should protect her especially, by the pleasant and beneficial (ones), from those that cause injury to the embryo.
notes: 'priyahitābhyām' is the instrumental dual of a dvandva, read 'by the pleasant and the beneficial (ones)'; the nouns are not in the text. 'garbhopaghātakarebhyaḥ' = from those (things) that harm the embryo (the following units list them).

hindi: जैसे-जैसे गर्भ वृद्धि को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे-वैसे भार, आहार और अपचार से, अनुमानित पाठ पर, स्त्री के बल का क्षय होता है।
english: As the embryo reaches growth, so, from the burden, the food and the error (apacāra), on a conjectural reading, there is loss of the woman's strength.

text_flags.why: possible: the syllable 'sa' is unexplained; 'bhāra-āhāra-apacārāt' (from burden, food and error) is a guess; 'bhāra-āhāra-sāpacārāt' (burden and food together with error) is also possible

notes: 'yathā yathā ... tathā tathā' means 'as ... so'. 'striyā' is regular sandhi for striyāḥ (visarga dropped before b). The member 'sa' in 'bhārāhārasāpacārāt' is unclear, so the reading of the ablative is conjectural. 'apacāra' = wrong conduct or error (in regimen); the text does not say of what.

hindi: इस विषय में ये गर्भ को हानि पहुँचाने वाले हैं।
english: In this matter, these are the (ones) causing injury to the embryo.
notes: GROUPING: 109, 110 ('tadyathā') and 111 form one statement and a list. Predicate is understood ('are').

hindi: वह जैसे —
english: Namely —
notes: Printed 'tadyathā' = tat + yathā, a formula introducing a list.

words.gloss: sexual intercourse (vyavāya); exertion (vyāyāma); emaciating (karśana); blow, injury (abhighāta); excessive; agitating; riding in vehicles
vehicle riding (repeated in print; possible slip)

keeping awake; day; sleep; natural urge; holding back; undigested (ajīrṇa); sun-heat; fire; anger; grief; fear; fright; fasting; squatting (utkaṭaka; probable); uneven; hard; seat or posture; pit; well; falling into; disagreeable; seeing; hearing; and so on

hindi: मैथुन, व्यायाम, दुबला करने वाला, चोट, अत्यधिक झटके देने वाली सवारी, रात में जागना, दिन में सोना, वेगों को रोकना, अजीर्ण यानी बिना पचा, धूप, आग, क्रोध, शोक, भय, घबराहट, उपवास, उकड़ूँ बैठना, ऊबड़-खाबड़ और कठोर आसन, गड्ढे और कुएँ में गिरना, अप्रिय का देखना और सुनना आदि।
english: Sexual intercourse (vyavāya), exertion (vyāyāma), emaciation (karśana), blows (abhighāta), excessively agitating riding in vehicles, keeping awake at night, sleep by day, holding back natural urges, undigested (food) (ajīrṇa), sun-heat, fire, anger, grief, fear, fright, fasting, squatting (utkaṭaka, probably), uneven and hard seats or postures, falling into a pit or well, seeing and hearing disagreeable (things), and so on.

text_flags.why: possible: 'yānayāna' looks like a doubled 'yāna'; 'rā' + 'trijāgaraṇa' (next token) is a split word 'rātri-jāgaraṇa'
certain enough: 'krogha' is not a word; 'krodha' (anger) fits the list between agni and śoka; the first 'tri' belongs with the previous token's 'rā' (rātri)

notes: A long dvandva list (items of the compound are read as separate items). The stray space 'yānarā trijāgaraṇa' is read as 'rātri-jāgaraṇa'. 'utkaṭaka' is probably a squatting posture (probable); 'utkaṭaviṣama' with a different division is possible. 'ajīrṇa' = undigested (ajīrṇa), read as undigested food. 'karśana' = emaciating, an adjective in the list. 'saṃkṣobhi' = agitating. The list is ended by 'ādayaḥ'. The doubled 'yāna' is not repeated in the translation. 'vyavāya' = sexual intercourse (standard). GROUPING: 111 completes 109-110.

hindi: संक्षेप में, सब अन्न और पान जो अत्यन्त भारी, गरम, तीक्ष्ण और रूखा हो, और कठोर चेष्टाएँ।
english: In brief, all food and drink that is excessively heavy, hot, sharp (tīkṣṇa) and dry, and harsh activities.

text_flags.why: certain: the colon is a printed stand-in for the visarga

notes: 'ati' is read to govern all four qualities (heavy, hot, sharp, dry). The sentence has no verb; it carries on the list of 111 ('these are causes of injury'), nothing is supplied. 'anna-pāna' (food and drink) is neuter singular as a dvandva.

hindi: तथा।
english: Likewise.
notes: GROUPING: introduces 114.

words.gloss: deity; rakṣas (demon); non-increase; protection; for the sake of

hindi: देवता, राक्षस और अनुपचय से रक्षा के लिए वह लाल वस्त्र न पहने, सवारी पर न चढ़े, मद्य यानी मादक पेय और मांस का सेवन न करे।
english: For the sake of protection from deities, rakṣas (demons) and non-increase (anupacaya), (she) should not wear red garments, should not mount a vehicle, should not consume madya (an intoxicating drink) and meat.

text_flags.why: possible: the doubled 't' is a print habit (as in other doubled consonants); 'raktāni' (red) is the word
possible: 'aśrīyāt' is not a form; 'aśnīyāt' (should eat) fits

notes: 'devatārakṣo'nupacayaparirakṣaṇārtham' is read as 'for the sake of protection from (harm by) deities, rakṣas, and non-increase'; the exact relation of the three members is not decided (they could also be read 'protection of the deities and rakṣas' share'). The subject 'she' (the pregnant woman) is understood from 106-107. 'madya-māṃsa' as a dvandva: madya (intoxicating drink) and meat (māṃsa). 'rakta' may mean red or dyed red; red is taken. GROUPING: follows 113.
